mc-plan 1
name: Whisper
request: Add a whisper(text) function in src/whisper.js that returns the text in lower case with three dots at the end. Export it from src/index.js with tests.
folder: wt2
base: main
app-name: word-tools: whisper
summary: word-tools is a small library of text helpers that programmers can use in their own code. This change adds a new helper called whisper. It takes a piece of text, makes the first letter a capital and everything else lower case, and adds "..." on the end, so "hELLO WORLD" becomes "Hello world...".
assumption: whisper follows the same pattern as capitalize: an ES module named export in its own file, src/whisper.js, re-exported from src/index.js, with a one-line doc comment.
assumption: Following the owner's change: only the very first character of the whole text is upper-cased. Everything after it is lower-cased, including the first letters of later words. "Hello World" becomes "Hello world...".
assumption: The capitalising rule is the same as the existing capitalize helper: upper-case text[0] and lower-case the rest. If the text starts with a space or punctuation, that character is left as is, so whisper(" hi") returns " hi...". It does not skip ahead to the first letter.
assumption: Non-string input throws a TypeError with the message "whisper expects a string". whisper checks this itself, so the message names whisper and not capitalize.
assumption: An empty string returns "...".
assumption: Three dots are always added, even if the text already ends with dots or other punctuation. whisper("Wait...") returns "Wait......".
assumption: The dots are three ASCII period characters ("..."), not the single ellipsis character (…).
assumption: Case changes use JavaScript's standard toUpperCase()/toLowerCase(), with no locale-specific rules.
assumption: The README gets a short whisper(text) section next to the capitalize one, so the new helper is documented.
assumption: Tests use the built-in node:test and node:assert/strict, like the existing tests, so no dependencies are added.
contract: This is a library, so it has no UI, routes or HTTP endpoints. The contract is the module API.
contract: Existing (do not change):
contract: src/capitalize.js exports capitalize(word). It upper-cases word[0], lower-cases the rest, returns "" for "", and throws TypeError("capitalize expects a string") for non-strings.
contract: src/index.js contains export capitalize from "./capitalize.js";.
contract: src/capitalize.test.js stays unchanged and must keep passing.
contract: package.json is an ES module ("type": "module"). The test script is node --test.
contract: New:
contract: File src/whisper.js has a named export export function whisper(text).
contract: If typeof text !== "string": throw new TypeError("whisper expects a string"). This check must come before any call to capitalize so the message is whisper's own.
contract: If text === "": return "...".
contract: Otherwise return text[0].toUpperCase() + text.slice(1).toLowerCase() + "...". Importing and reusing capitalize from "./capitalize.js" after the type check is fine, because it gives the same result.
contract: src/index.js adds the line export whisper from "./whisper.js"; and keeps the capitalize export.
contract: Test file src/whisper.test.js imports test from "node:test", assert from "node:assert/strict", and whisper from "./index.js" (the entry point, not ./whisper.js).
contract: Example values: whisper("hELLO") === "Hello..."; whisper("Hello World") === "Hello world..."; whisper("hELLO wORLD") === "Hello world..."; whisper("SHH") === "Shh..."; whisper("already quiet") === "Already quiet..."; whisper("") === "..."; whisper("Wait...") === "Wait......"
contract: README.md gets a section ## whisper(text) placed before ## Tests, stating that whisper("hELLO wORLD") returns "Hello world...".

feature: whisper-function
title: Add whisper(text) and export it from the package entry point
story: As a developer using word-tools, I want a whisper(text) helper that I can import from the package entry point. It should return my text with only the first letter capitalised, everything else in lower case, and three dots on the end.
kind: mechanical
check: Importing whisper from src/index.js gives a function
check: whisper("hELLO") returns "Hello..."
check: whisper("Hello World") returns "Hello world..." (only the first letter of the whole text is capitalised, not the first letter of every word)
check: whisper("hELLO wORLD") returns "Hello world..."
check: whisper("SHH") returns "Shh..."
check: whisper("already quiet") returns "Already quiet..."
check: whisper("") returns "..."
check: whisper("Wait...") returns "Wait......" (dots are always added, even if the text already ends with dots)
check: whisper(" hi") returns " hi..." (only the very first character is upper-cased, so a leading space stays a space)
check: whisper(42) throws a TypeError with message "whisper expects a string"
check: whisper(undefined) throws a TypeError
check: The existing capitalize tests still pass, and capitalize is still exported from src/index.js
check: src/whisper.test.js exists and npm test exits with code 0
